I loved this game for what it was. I just played it all out in the small time I had. I love that gritty real-life stuff in games like back when Cart Life (the food cart simulator) had the relentless fortitude to provide an intentionally awful experience, but in the realm of learning and the drive to succeed. Running out of gas in this game in the freeway, flipping your car, having to repair/replace parts to get to a destination. Paying for parts. Staying in a motel. It was all lovely. It just seemed so blocky. It seemed predictable very fast and the fun factor left very fast with the tedium of the entire game.
The dialogue was reminescent of Jazzpunk and I loved having to keep a car maintained, but there were no upgrades (aside from a few iffy ones), there was no real goal. There was no story. There was no purpose to keep going.
I know it's early access and I will continue to watch the development, but as of right now, I can not recommend it. A demo would suffice to see what is up, but for the sake of purchasing, not yet.

I rarely write a review for a game, except this is one of my favourite franchise, the HITMAN series. Yes, i was very exciting when Hitman Absolution release after how Blood Money made me feel like the best game i've played. If you never know why Hitman series is greater than other stealth games, let me tell you:
- Free of choices, you kill target with many ways you can think of, a silent assassin or a rampage killer, up to you.
- Disguise, the signature of this series, you can disguise anyone and freely walk around to plan your assassinate.
- Level design, large and complex, you need to learn the whole map before acting.
Ok, back to Absolution, at first, i was really impressed: Beatiful enviroment, introduce instinct system (cool, but I always play at hardest mode, so it not so important for me). And a storyline, yeah, at least they try to tell you a story instead of a contract killer. But as i play throught out the missions, it start to reveal it is not the Hitman i used to play. Let's check back what make the series great and compare with this game:
- Free of choices: NO, you still have some options to assassinate target, but these are what the dev give you, not yours. You cant choose weapons at the beginning, you cant keep weapons that you found, you can only use what the dev give you on each level. So this is a basic stealth game, you come from A to B, take some thing you need, then do the mission, very straight foward.
- Disguise: Really annoying since the new detect system make you very hard to roaming freely. The instinct may help a bit, but gone real fast that you cant relie on. If you killing some one to recover instinct, you're punished by the system point that's really annoying too. Hey, you're a most dangerous Hitman, how come people judge you by killing someone (negative score) that's not a target.
- Level desgin: almost disappoint, small and very straight foward, you come from A to B to complete the level, and always sneek like other stealth games.
What keep me still playing this game? The Storyline, which is made like an action movie with slow motion and characters design is good. That's all. Checkpoint is useless and buggy, everytime i reload a checkpoint, the screen turns red (i play on AMD Radeon R9 270, which AMD is optimize for this game, what a joke).
Sorry folks, but NO.

I never expected to have to see this game again - especially not on Steam.
I used to play this game - a lot in fact. I used to play is so often that I was on the leaderboard for goodness knows how long. In fact, I'm probably still there if I ever feel the need to log back on, which I can promise everyone here, I won't.
The game is riddiculous, the moderators were awful (I assume they must have been replaced by now at the very least) the developers are obvious cash grabbers and the community itself is downright toxic.
Not once have I been so dissapointed by the Greenlight system to actually begin to condemn it.
But enough about my life story, let's get down to business.
The game is P2W and I think that's obvious to everybody who has played the game for longer than an hour. In fact, I spent quite a jolly well amount on this game over the years that I played. The chances of somebody acquiring enough cash and coins to be able to compete with the top players is just stupidly low. If anything, the best chance you have is if you befriended an incredibly skilled player so that you can mooch off of that person during the tournaments, even then it would take weeks if not months to have enough to purchase anything worthwhile.
The developers are an absolute joke: I left the game approximately a year ago and I took a look today just so I could make this review on Steam and the updates are just so damn awful it's an embarrasment. From what I can see is that they've added more guns and made the place look pretty along with a couple of incredibly dull gamemodes which aren't worth anybody's time.
I noticed a few reviews earlier complaining about the farming and cheating. I generally believe that to be overhyped nonsense in most games myself, but this time it's actually true. In fact, it's so bad that the developers created a system where players find other players who cheat or hack and are rewarded for doing so.  I remember it being so bad that I along with the majority of the population were having to complain to the moderators who simply were not fixing this issue and rewarding people their well deserved money. Bare in mind that these were 20 odd pages of this stuff. I'm not even going to bother counting the amount of reports there.
The moderators themselves were an absolute joke. Again, I'm basing this on the previous moderators so they're probably different people now. One fellow who managed to become a moderator was simply because he was a popular fellow within the game. He was a 15 year old child. You don't give children that amount of power over people - and he was no exception. Another fellow who was a moderator was somebody who I had never even heard of. Do bare in mind that the community was very close to one another even if they were a bunch of toxic individuals who I'd never offer a cup of tea to, so this came as a surprise to me. What happened? This individual became easily the worst moderator I have ever seen to date - laziness was out of this world. I can only hope these two are gone for the community's sake at the very least.
Community is toxic - I don't think I ever had a day during my years of playing without being insulted repeatedly on a daily basis. Now you can remove the chatting function so you don't have to read people's comments, but it does become rather tiresome after a while. It's a child's game, not that that's a bad thing, but it's run by children for children. Expect extremely childish comments to be made.
The clan system is pointless. I did run several top clans at one point or another. In fact, I remember it very well indeed. They were the only reason I stayed around for so long, eventually I just got tired and left however, one can only stand so much boredom in a game. There were tournaments which took place which were interesting even if I didn't take part in any of them for my own reasons.
But of course, I leave the worst till last. My opinion as to why the game is essentially dead: comboing and flag farming. People level up too quickly and leave the game immediately after. I was one of the few people at the time who never did any of these things. In fact, I even had a clan which was completely against either of these things. You did any of that, and you'd be gone without a second's hesitation I abhore it and I find it pathetic that the developers thought that this should have been allowed to occur even when they knew this game was dying. Absolutely shameful and I feel no pity for them whatsoever. They brought it on themselves.
Honestly, this game shouldn't be worth anybody's time. I have no ill feelings towards it in the slightest, but it simply isn't worth it. P2W, awful developers and obviously a cash-grab. I'm sure the only reason it's still running is because of people paying money because of simple nostalgia.
I loved it at one point, and it helped me through a lot of problems, but God damn is it a joke that it's still around and on Steam of all places.
2/10 and this will be the last day I ever open TDP4 again for any reason.
And if anybody wants to know who I am, I'm sure you can figure it out eventually.

LONG REVIEW! (copy-pasted from a post I made elsewhere. I made a few changes, however)
TL;DR: Pay-to-play microtransaction game. Community is abhorrent, staff are ignorant hypocrites.
The following amounts of $ are based off the Kongregate prices from ~1 year ago, and are estimated. I am not checking to see if the prices have changed, because this game disgusts me, and I passionately refuse to play it.
I played this game for about 2 years. It quickly became very very P2W. DO NOT PLAY THIS GAME. The gameplay itself is good, but past about level 12 it becomes extremely P2W. You can acquire effectively 3x or 4x more health and armor than your enemies by paying about $25, and get twice as much every stat by paying roughly $50. And then the high majority of guns cost over $15 or $20 each. About 60+ cash, and 40k+coins, which will cost roughly $25. And if you don't buy those yourself, I can completely guarantee that you will be dominated by someone with the defence and the health. You would not beat them even if it was 6v1. I played this game for 2 or 3 years because I had friends on it, and the gameplay itself was fun, mostly because I had these weapons and bonuses. But it is completely pay to win, and I quit it ages ago. There is a slot machine, and the prizes are: 50, 300, 500 coins, 3, 5 cash. (don't know chance but you never seem to gain money if you do it for a while) Besides that, the only reward is the best gun in the game. But the chance of getting it is below 0.001%. A TDP4 moderator known as LiP was supposed to of said this. To back it up, I spent approximately 400 cash (sold all my guns and bonuses and quit the game for good) and didn't get the gun. (I know many people who spent over 1000)
Also, each day you come on, you get to open a briefcase with a very high chance of getting the highest bonus. The bonus of getting a discount on buying things in the game.
The reason the game rating is high, is based off the Kongregate rating.
The reason the rating from high is just an educated guess. The reason is because most of the people are new, rate it after maybe an hour of playing. Game-sites in my experience tend not to have reviewers,critics, and long time gamers like Steam does. They rate it after about an hour of playing, then they either stop playing, or they pay for bonuses and weapons, and don't touch the rating. Neither group touches the ratings, until the realize like so many people including myself has about the obvious truth. The gameplay itself is good, and it is enjoyable. But once you see the community, and you get to the P2W time, it's just over.
Most of the community are jerks, complaining about killsteals, noobs, hackers, buyers, etc. It's one of the games where if you use the wrong gun, or if you use a certain tactic, you will be cussed out, called a hacker, etc. Most of them will just call you a b**** for killing them twice in a row. The main demographic of the community is Russian. (I'm not trying to be prejudiced towards the Russian nationality, I'm just stating the demographic)
The developers are pretty careless. There is a glitch where you can shoot 2-5 bullets from almost any weapon, including the best snipers in the game, and the very high majority of the medium level+ players use this "tactic." There is a glitch where if you hold down 2 buttons, you lag out the game for everyone,(easily 4000 ping) (plenty of people do this) resulting in a game crash, and disconnection. These people are 90% of the time never banned, from my knowledge. I will confirm with my friend who used to be a moderator (not saying his name) for confirmation. The admins are extremely lenient with certain aspects of their terms and conditions. For example, it basically says "no killfarming" in their Terms & Conditions, yet literally any time you go on the game, you'll find at least 5-40 rooms obviously named something related to a kill-farm. People killfarm in order to get KDR, cash, and coins, because they can't earn it legitimately due to the game being P2W. Yet I got banned for doing a combo before, despite 3 moderators disagreeing with the ban. One of my friends in the room was accused of being a bot...Despite playing for the past year, and typing plenty, etc. He had no affiliation or connection to my name, and we lived in completely different countries, so we should of had quite different I.P addresses. It is also stated in the terms & conditions that: (simply put) one is not allowed to killfarm/combo in order to gain XP, currenc, kills, etc. However, there are constantly multiple combos going on in the game, and absolutely no staff members do anything about it. There are other examples of this, too.
If you played TDP4 and you are wondering who I am, my username was xXDeath42Xx. I owned the 4th largest clan ever made in that game called PIE, (3369 members at its peak) yet most of them have quit, and it is very slowly dying. This is the most P2W game I have ever seen in my life. It is also the worst game I've ever played, and I regret playing it.

If you are here because you saw Puzzle Quest, and don't have a burning interest in playing the next Marvel game, I suggest you turn back and play Puzzle Quest 1 or 2.
If you are here for the Marvel Universe, and have no idea what puzzle quest is, then you COULD like it.
This game is a match-3 type game, much in the same vein as Candy Crush, Bejewled, and like it's namesake, Puzzle Quest.
It says it's a work in progress, so I'll give the dev's the benefit of the doubt, that they'll fix the game's problems. I have played Puzzle Quest 1, own it on 360, steam, ds, and the iOS. I own Puzzle Quest 2, and Galactrix for the DS. And now I have played this game, on steam. So I know what the games are like, and what they have done.
I have also played Geomancer, the match-3 game from Square-Enix, but I have not touched Candy crush, because that game has no depth beyond "HEY LOOK AT ME I GOT THIS SCORE AND MY E-PEEN IS HUGE", much like bejeweled. I like my RPG's, thanks.
I don't mind the direction they took this game in, where they add in an active attack each match. Previously, you would only attack the enemy when you would match attack gems. Otherwise, the other gems were resources to power your abilites.
But where this gets confusing is when they do not make clear various aspects of the game, such as when the opponent goes. If you're attacking all the time, will your opponent just not get an attack, and just fill up their resource gems like in Geomancer? And what about attacking the enemy who has the strongest weapon? Will his ability get taken out, so that they can't use it? These are gameplay issues that should be addressed. When your user is CONFUSED on different aspects of your CORE gameplay in the beginning of the game, that doesn't bode well for them continuing to play it and 'experiment' to find out all the rules to the game.
Micro-transactions are an okay model. I mean, after all, this IS a free game. I have not tested the viability of different heroes, nor the abilities that come with them, so I can't comment on how balanced it is. But based on what I have read in the other reviews, it seems that it's not looking too good. I would recommend doing research on it yourself.
All in all, I expected the game to be way better, but it's medocore at best. A new direction for Puzzle Quest, not necessarily good, but not really bad either. This game didn't catch my interest beyond the novel idea that Marvel and PQ came together, so I got bored of it quickly, once that novelty wore off.
In terms of Quality, I would rate the games like so:
1) Puzzle Quest.
2) Puzzle Quest 2.
3) Geomancer / this game.
4) Galactrix.

Winded Review:
First of all, if you are interested in this game hoping it will play like X sandbox game, expunge that notion from your mind right now. There are several reasons for this. Even among apples there are different varieties and you may not like Golden Delicious apples but go wild for Fuji apples. Same goes for games of a similar genre. In addition, this game is farily new when compared with other popular 2d sandbox type games (i.e. Terraria) and so it is frankly unfair to judge based on that. Would be like deciding if you like a cake based on the taste of the flower you plan to use.
The game has its bugs. The developers are focusing on dealing with the bugs rather than pushing out a lot of new content.
New things (monsters/features/etc) are slipped in as well to keep things interesting. But they have also overhauled the system a few times already. (The most current UI I am not a fan of, but it was an improvement over the previous.)
I should be far more professional about this review and listing the various problems. But despite the problems I find, I still enjoy the game very much.
If you are able to get over the idea that it isn't, "just like x game" you will probably enjoy it as well.
If you are capable of understanding the game is in it's early infancy (release wise), you will probably enjoy the game.
If you need a game that tells you what to do next, you will find yourself not enjoying the game.
If you base a game's enjoyment based on how difficult it is, you may not enjoy the game very much.

Pretty good game, the game doesn't really hold up to the standard of the classic DK but is still very enjoyable.
+Good Campaign, both the Vanilla and DLC campaign had quite a couple missions which had good build-up, were well-constructed and alot of fun to play
+The narrator: Well written and quite funny to listen to.
+Worker AI works very well, workers prioritize tasks very well even though you don't really have a whole lot of control over it yourself.
+Lots of control over your dungeon. You can fill up corridors back up, you decide where you put your tools, you can even restructure your entire dungeon if you have enough money.
~Unit variation is alright, every factions has 4 different unit types with each 3 different tiers each and potential tactics you can create with that. Problem is that fights are way too quick for you to use any real tactics like assassinating with stealth units
~Faction System: Instead of 1 big faction there are now 2(+1 with DLC). While this brings some variation in game style(although not that much) the Demon faction had only 2, potentially 3, missions while the Horde factions has like 7
-Bland Specializations: On topic of faction variation, while I think the Horde faction was ok, the Undead Faction really lacks the feeling of actually playing undead, sure, they are better at resurrecting their soldiers then the other factions but unlike DK 2 you can't actually turn fallen enemies into soldiers like the Skeleton or Vampire in DK 2, which I think really should have been one of it's pointers. Same with demons, they have a torture room but it's essentially useless, you can't convert enemies like you could in the old games.
-It's somewhat tedious to click on things with the hand-cursor, frequently missing or selecting wrong monsters
-While I liked the narrator, the story and setting itself are quite cartoon'ish and unserious, almost all the characters and even alot of the story are quite obviously a parody of popular high-fantasy settings like Lord of the Rings, Game of Thrones and World of Warcraft.
Despite it's flaws I liked it quite alot. I should however mention that I bought it at a 75% sale and I would really only recommend you to buy it in a sale, it's not really worth €55 euros(with DLC). It's more of a Indie game so €15 is a more appropriate price.

+research
+stats and skills
+huge choice of weapons and at least a few possible fighting styles

+magic
+nice soundtrack
+some enemies are challenging
Cons:

I wont lie, this game has blown my expectations out of the metaphorical water. I haven't played long enough yet to give a full review but after 5 hours I have to say this is like a lovechild of Elite Dangerous and Red Dead Redemption (gameplay wise) and also Starcraft and Cowboy Bebop theme wise. It also feels like it could be an extension of the Mass Effect universe.
The developers have really focused on perfecting the basic core mechanics that are both simple and have a lot of longevity. I think this is the kind of game you could enjoy for a long time.
I've owned this game for quite a while and I never touched it until now and I'm really glad I did. If you're out there and you're on the fence about this game I promise you it is very easy to start. You wont be looking up tutorials unless you want to.
Update: After 26 hours I'm finally putting the game down. It was a great journey and whilst the story was nothing special, if you enjoy building up a character from scratch then you'll love this game. As I progressed I felt stronger and stronger but some of that was lost because as you progress to further and further areas the enemies get stronger with you. Whenever I visited earlier systems I was always reminded of my progress though.
I think if you were to play this strategically and focused on min-maxing your ship, you could easily get 100+ hours out of this game.
Overall a fantastic SCI-FI game and a must buy for people who enjoy starting with nothing and earning a spot at the top.

I've gone through what seems to be an endless list of patches till this day of posting and still the game is still able to astound me with the constant bugs.
Critical: 5 BSOD events during playing the game itself. Playing the older Grid 2 yields hours of interrupted gameplay, or anything else for that matter. Then lose all your progress from starting the game before the crash.
Cons:
1. AI: Can concur with most that the AI is behaving in an unruly manner, especially ones by Ravensport. What's more as easily they can spin you out, you can't retaliate effectively by PIT because they seem to be immune from pushing?
2. Downforce + Grip: I can expect the Touring cars to be slidy, but a F312 Dallara acts like its driving on ice. Or things one would expect to have more default downforce. Also AI seems to be able to slide at speed, while player cannot.
3. Tuning: Inital mid level tuning is too coarse for some courses. It should be full tuning at all times or never at all. Tuning is
also a cure for the poor grip/downforce on the F312 for example.
4. The nag everytime a season ends. If I wanted it to be harder, I would be playing Asseto Corsa with a phone keypad. Or drive a real car. Just saying.
5. Endurance: At the shortest length, the tyre wear is overly much. If it happened in real life, you would sue the tyre company. Also losing grip means driftiness, but the controls won't allow finessed drifting, thus crashes occur.
Pros: 1. First time I had an opportunity to drive Aussie V8 supercars. I now understand why the country is divided into before races.
2. Discipline variety: Keep alternating to relive the tedium of driving on the same tracks in every possible direction. Like the old days of NFS underground. Surprisingly apart from the speed, one can drive the same way  between all categories.
Since I would not be able to finish the game without crashes every other race, this game is a reminder of my own folly of buying a pre-order sim from CM ever.

So I had one go at this game and I'm already amazed. I survived for only 16 days until everyone of my crew died. My crew consisted of Pavle, Bruno and Marko. Scavanging for stuff was hard since some people went there from before. Our house didn't have any food and it was cold. So I did almost everything to survive. I got a lot of food, medication, and building supplies. I was set to survive for a long time, but raiders. They steal everything. This game is hard and that's more enjoyable. This game even showed me how I'm a monster. Whilst svanging for items, I entered a house and there was an elderly couple. Seeing as to how they were unarmed, I took everything they had and ran, without any second thoughts. The person I used to steal that stuff was Marko (i used him to scavange stuff everytime). He became broken, he refused to do anything, so I had the rest of the team to talk with him. Soon I got another person to join us, Cveta. She didn't last long. Once night approached on the same day she arrived. I took her to scavange some stuff and she died. There was one armed man there who didn't like me snooping into his stuff. Soon after that everone was depressed. Things got harder as well since bandits kept stealing our stuff. I took Bruno for a run since no one wanted to do anything (Marko and Pavle) and I took him to this church. Everyone there was armed. I managed to take out one guy but my weapon broke and the other guy shot me. One the morning came Marko took off and it was just Pavle. I managed to make him survive 1 day until he became depressed and refused to scavange for supplies. Then the last night some raiders came in and they shot him. He got lethally wounded and he didn't make it to see morning.
I was honestly mad at Marko for being depressed from stealing from people (he also had to kill someone before that since I panicked). I liked Bruno since he only thought about surviving, he usually says stuff like "As long as we have supplies, doesn't matter who we kill". On the other hand Pavle and Marko would be sad at what happened and they won't forget about it. This game comes to show you how hard life is at war, and how it can change some people. I will try to survive again, this time with Bruno, Roman and Arica.

There are not many things to say about this masterpiece. It's a game that has its own personality, making it differ from the rest survival games.
Depressing atmosphere in conjuction with simple but clever gameplay elements and beatiful soundtrack. There are some difficult choices that you don't face often in video games. Would you help an old couple by giving some of your food and medicine and making your members try to survive harder? Would you try to save a helpless girl from the hands of a dangerous armed man while you are empty handed? Tough choices that become even tougher since the death of a character is permanent.
Highly recommend it to those who want to experience the cruelty and the hardships of war in a different way than the other action games.

First of all, this is the first game ever I can remember where I actually viewed the credits, I just had to know who'd made this game, wich says quite alot about my impressions of it. All unknown people for me though, but that doesn't take away any of the splendor of this game.
As a game, I'm overwhelmed that it portraits the war from the view of the civilians. On top of that, it's not an easy game either. My first impressions made me think of the old classic "the lost patrol" in how you experienced your characters:
Always short on food, getting wounds that become worse, never enough equipment (and I really mean never), and even though you know there's probably an end somewhere, it just eludes you. All focus is on what's most important for the moment.
The game layout itself is simple enough, very easy to learn and get used to, but that doesn't mean it is in any way an easy game. On the contrary, no ability to save when you want and re-load (everyting is autosaved as you progress), no difficulty settings to adjust to make certain points of the game easier, and no clear hints as to what to do or what will work actually makes this game all Ironman mode. You're holed up in your house, and you just have to explore your surroundings to get the most out of it, whatever way you can.
As a hoarder in games, I do enjoy gathering and scavanging stuff, but some of the frustration in this game comes from the fact that you never can bring back everything you find, at the most maybe one third. You'll just have to figure out what you for the moment need most and what you can make the most of. Alot of stuff will be left behind.
Finally, there's events as well, so you not only need to feed, rest and make sure there's coffee and tobacco enough for all, but acting in a bad manner towards your neighbours for example might have an impact on your morale.
If you're interested in exploring, managing, crafting and do just whatever it requires to get through each and every day, this most definetly is a game for you. I rate it 10/10, no doubt.

This game has an excellent crafting system, a decent scavenging and trade system, and an okay fighting system. The fighting system could use some work, but it isn't a fighting game as such.
It has a decent story - text isn't too long, and maybe just a bit too short at times. Yes, some people call the writing infantile, but I prefer the term simple.
It has a few kinks here and there, but tells a good story.
The only improvement I would like to see is an addition to when the survivors are doing very well for themselves - once you have all the weapons, food, fuel, water, etc... you might need, and are nearly impervious to attacks and just waiting for the war to end, I think that the survivors/civilians should actually get involved with the war. It feels like a side-show at times - you're affected by the war, but not really involved. The reality is that while not everyone is a soldier, civilians can and do get involved in wars. Once you have all these resources, that's when you can have group dynamics start falling apart because one of them wants to go out and support the militia actively while the others just want to stay hidden. And what happens after the war then, when the militia loses and your guy has been out killing dozens of soldiers and civilians for the militia?
That's the only group-dynamic lacking in this game: Actual involvement in the war, one way or another, as opposed to just scavenging, trading and the occasional skirmish.

While it may seem like yet another bad MOBA at a glance, Battlerite will be a fairly new and refreshing experience for a lot of players. There's no creeps, no bases to defend, no leveling up or buying items; just high-skill arena combat. You move your character with WASD and aim skills with the mouse, rather than moving with right-click like a typical MOBA. Either way it's free so you might as well give it a shot.
Good:
- It's free without being "pay to win"
- High skill ceiling and mechanically deep
- Gameplay is satisfying, matches are quick and entertaining
- Developers gradually balance with small tweaks rather than knee-jerk changes
- The rate at which you unlock content is very fair, never feels like "grinding"
- Useful replay system, but viewing them outside of the game would be nice
Questionable:
- "Battlerite" system is underwhelming, feels like the illusion of choice*
- Not all characters available immediately, you must earn them by playing
- Hard for new players to get into - no singleplayer mode, tutorial is misleading
- Many cosmetics look atrocious to the point of destroying the game's aesthetic
- Art-style feels generic and uninspired, very "Blizzard-esque" in a boring way
- Bloodline Champions was better (before it was abandoned, at least)
- Not enough variety in map layouts, arenas feel very samey as well
- Developers added some weird MOBA-esque mode... not sure why
* = Most characters have around 3 or 4 Battlerites that are pretty much manditory to get in all situations, and the remaining choices are decided by the enemy's composition moreso than player preference. Missing certain Battlerites will feel like your character is missing one of their arms: they just don't function properly without them. Before you had to pick 1 Battlerite per round, allowing you to adapt to the enemy's builds, but now you pick them all upfront which makes the system seem rather pointless.

I have recently bought GRID autosport, which probably means that i am not going to be playing GRID 2 very regularly as i have migrated to playing autosport, so i decided that i would write a review, seeing as i was rather close to 100 hours so i think i know what im talking about, or atleast mostly.
GRID 2 is an amazing game, probably the best racing game that i am yet to play, other than the new release of GRID which is infact GRID autosport. There are so many features and aspects that i like about GRID 2, but im not going to list them all as i would be going on forever, so im going to keep them blunt, short but informative at the same time.
Things i liked about the game:
--------------------------------
The controls: The controls took me a matter of minutes to get use to, and from there i was able to drive nice and smoothly, without having to worry about pressing the wrong button on my remote. (I believe you can also use a steering wheel for this game).
The detail/graphics: The maps, the cars, the road, even the cones. you name it. Everything looks brilliant. The reflections on the cars are brilliant, and this detail is consistent throughout the whole game, and the graphics that they have produced, can even run on my computer which i am suprised about. The game is not slow or laggy whatsoever, meaning that you can have a very smooth racing experience, but at the same time have a lovely eyesite of distant mountains, as you control your car.
Music: The game has a variety of different tracks that are played throughout the game. The loading music, the main menu music, the racing music, all of it is of a high standard, and is great to listen to, and really makes you feel like your driving a car.
AI: The AI of this game are great. The WSR campaign, which is pretty much a singleplayer mode, is absolutely realistic, due to the fact that the computer drivers have been programmed so good. When driving, the way that the drivers move and think are so lifelike, and occasionally challenge you if you do in-fact smash into the back of there car, but i wouldn't try it.
Handling: All of the cars are tuned to perfection, and getting use to each type of handling, which each of the cars uniquely have is done with ease.
Multiplayer: Although the multiplayer is on the verge of becoming dead, its still great fun when playing with a full lobby, and the feeling of taking another persons car out after them doing it before hand is beautiful. (Not that thats how you should drive.)
Bad points about the game:
-----------------------------
What are you talking about? There are no bad points about this game! Despite all the people that have played GRID 2 and complained about it, i think that they should simply realise that codemasters took their time making this, as it is truly a masterpiece, and an experience that i am never going to forget. The game is absolutely brillaint, and upon buying GRID autosport which was released shortly after im reviewing this, i cannot wait to carry on with the next game in the series. Thank you so much codemasters for bringing us this game, and i would like to thank you for also releasing Autosport, as so far it is brilliant. Thank you, and i hope that this review has influenced anyone that is planning on buying the game.

I've been playing this game on my android since it was released, I've easily put 50 hours into the game, I have 25 roster slots, over ten heroes that are Lv30+ all without spending a dollar. Don't put this game down for microtransactions since you don't need to spend a dollar with all the rewards the tournametns and the PvE gives you.
-Update-
I still see people are complaining about the Microtransactions.
1) If you play the game daily roughly 2 hours a day and do all the missions in the PVE events and PVP a couple times a day you should get roughly 3,000-5,000 Iso-8, the tool to level up your characters. It costs roughly 20k Iso-8 to max out any 1* Hero and roughly 80k to max out a 2* hero. You will be able to max out any 1* or 2* character within weeks of just playing a couple hours a day.
2. You will also roughly get a few hundred Hero Points in the process, if you are starting out the game. Use them on the 100 Daily Deal Heroic pack. That is how you max out your 2*s. If you have played the game for a while, save the Hero Points for Alliance slots, or join an open alliance. I created a 20 person alliance and only spent twenty bucks on it, I could have waited a month for the same ammount of Hero Points. ((Some people spent a hundred))
3. Now for the 3* covers, playing a lot in any tournament or event will nail you 1-3 3* covers of one hero. You will also get covers through the Heroic Packs and any other special pack that you spend your free hero points on. They require alot of Iso-8 to max out. 170k for a rough estimate. HOWEVER the final level still requires only 2500 iso-8, which is something you can easily get within an hour.
4. Guys this isn't a game that you get Lv100 of all the strongest characters within hours of playing. This game is set up more of an MMO where you have to do the slow grind to get to that point. I don't mind it. I currently have 5 maxed out 2* Characters at Lv85, 3 maxed out 1* characters and I have a handful of other 2 and 3* characters over lv50 with two that I just need to grind all the way to max level. I've only spent fifty bucks on this game because I actually felt like it. I didn't feel like I needed to in order to continue this game. To compare with other games I've played, I put almost a thousand bucks in to League of Legends and I had put six hundred bucks into Dungeon Fighter Online before that got shut down. I probably could spend more money into this game, but I don't.

RCT has risen and fallen, and while it would seem that its mantle has been faithfully picked up by Planet Coaster, RCT2 will always hold a special place in my heart. The original RCT may as well have invented the "Tycoon" genre. Yes, there were competitors and RCT was not the first simulation game, but there's a reason no one remembers its competitors and why it seemed like after RCT every simulation game for the next 5 years had Tycoon in the title.
The original RCT gave creative freedom to build whatever your imagination desired along with a set of increasingly challenging scenarios to test your strategy and management skills. RCT 2 perfected this formula. More coasters, more themes, more track options, more modes, more everything. Plus you could play with actual Six Flags and they finally added a straight sandbox.
My gaming childhood was built on Smash Bros. and Rollercoaster Tycoon. RCT is the game that started it all. This is the only game in the series that's better in every way.

Having played over 80 hours of this game (majority of it in the beta branch) and seen the dev at work I can safely say that, what this game currently lacks in difficulty and content, the dev makes up for in dedication in fixing and improving the game and willingness to help those who need it.
This game has potential, lots of it, it just needs some time to grow.
Starting off the review with that.
Crea is a game with the same base structure as games like Terraria and Starbound, but they are not the same games, with over 700 hours of game time on Terraria, I will admit I went into Crea expecting it to be a lot like it, I was wrong and was punished for it, numerous times.
You will die in this game, with more slowpaced combat that almost requires the use of your trusty shield to survive, until later on in the game, more on that in a bit.
The combat mechanics as of right now is a bit like Dark Souls if I may; bait, counter and repeat.
However if you decide to use the bow or magic, combat sadly becomes a little bit too easy, the game is too nice when it comes to projectiles, they are too slow and are easy to predict, bosses suffer greatly from this.
With that, let us talk about a weak point of the game, the difficulty.
When you first start, the game will seem to be very difficult and you will die at least once in the first 15 minutes.
But once you get experience, unlock a few skills and naturally get better, you will notice that, hey, this isn't so hard?
The balancing in this game is sadly something that definitely needs attention somewhere down the line, especially so when it comes to bosses, all bosses can be done naked, as long as you have a weapon that is up to date.
The bosses die too quick and their attacks are of no threat, due to what I mentioned earlier, projectiles are too slow.
They have a long wind up time before they start moving, and when they finally start moving, they are too slow.
It's possible to one shot the last boss with a bow with the right build.
Content wise the game sadly is lacking as well, it's there, but lacking, but I trust that I will edit this review later and change this. :)
There are 4 bosses, something called Horde Realms which is something that has a chance to spawn after killing something called a xxx Spawner of all mobs in the game, they are kind of like mini dungeons that only consist of the mob that spawned the realm portal.
There are also dungeons, great for leveling and loot, pretty standard, they function a bit like ARPG dungeons, in that they have various "quests", for example "Pacifist" meaning, don't kill any mobs, and bonuses/penalties, for example increased/decreased experience.
EDIT: With the recent patch adding enchantment, the gearing up part has become a great deal more fun.
Trying out different enchantment builds is very fun, especially using the more unique ones!
Loot wise, there's a few different tiers and variations for each weapon type (sword, bow and wand) as well as armor.
Generally there's three different weapon and armor sets per tier that you can craft, one for each type of weapon.
There's also scrolls that can be researched, I've only found one weapon scroll, a sword, as well as a bunch of different accessories.
Bosses also have a chance to drop unique weapons and accessories, same with Horde Realms that seem to all have something unique.
Crafting, the crafting in this game is more in-depth than Terraria, in that you have various skills to increase the quality of equipment before you run out of "Balance", for people who've played FFXIV A Realm Reborn, the system will feel very familiar.
It could use some looking into, it's very easy to get max quality right now.
Does require some thinking but not enough I believe.
EDIT: Recent patch made the crafting significantly harder, sound like a bad thing? Nah, much better this way. :P
Bugs, yes, this game has them, like any other game, but the dev is very dedicated in solving them, and has made great progress on the beta branch of the game.
The most jarring bug right now that some people seem to experience, is a bug that makes water mobs fly away.
Personally haven't experienced this after the last patch on beta, though some people still do it seems.
EDIT: With the most recent patch, a lot of bugs were fixed, mobs flying away being one of them. :P
Anyway, I've gone on long enough, Terraria fanboys can downvote as much as they want.
The game has potential and I'm looking forward to see where the game goes from here.

Let's talk about a little something called the "Call of Duty" effect.
There's a strange thing that happens whenever Treyarch make another Call of Duty game - the campaign is terrible. You see, the story of a Call of Duty game really just feels like it takes a back seat to the gameplay, while the gameplay just feels like it's there to drive the story along. We could compare this to Half-Life 2, where the gameplay feels crisp, fun, and always changing, or to something like Spec Ops: The Line, where the monotony of the gameplay is actually meant to add just one more layer to the dark and twisted story. Call of Duty takes the worst of both, and makes it into a campaingn.
Homefront suffers greatly from the Call of Duty effect, and, given the fact that the game was sold mainly for its campaign, this is a pretty bad problem.
Gameplay in this game feels awful. It's nothing but a linear set of shooting galleries with your squad mates constantly yelling at you to do the same things over and over until you do them. The shooting feels awful (enemies take a little too long to die, gun recoil is almost nonexistent, the visual of most sights on the guns make it look like you're shooting through JPEGS, the sounds of the guns are just awful and unfulfilling), and there is no other gameplay aside from a couple "do this to move on" sequences.
Meanwhile, the characters are just as bad. The characters are "memorable" in the sense that they have names and they have about one defining trait each (the really swear-y Jimmy Hopkins, the really innocent woman, the former soldier, and the Korean techie). There is no backstory or intrigue provided to any of the characters, no character arcs, nothing to make us want to get to know them or be with them at all. There's no chemistry between them either, as it becomes very apparent very quickly that their lines were all recorded at separate times in separate rooms.
To round it off, the storyline is weak and boring. Yes, you get a couple interesting set pieces and scripted events (Call of Duty is famous for something, after all), but most of the time you don't even know what you're doing until you're actually doing it. On one mission we were told that a friend of ours had some sort of plan. On the next mission, we learned that the plan somehow involved taking a chopper. On the mission after, we learn that we're going to use the chopper to steal some jet fuel tankers from an enemy convoy. It's just a stream-of-consciousness story - it never explains why we're doing something or what we're trying to accomplish until it's time to actually accomplish it. On the flip side, it never gives us a proper sense of threat - we don't have a real feel for what we stand to lose, and we have almost zero sense of how powerful the enemy is at any given time (because we're able to easily shoot our way out of every fight).
This game is a boring script read by boring people in order to outline a poorly paced story, and is garnished with absolutely godawful and unmemorable gameplay.
On the plus side, at least it's only 4 hours long (I have 6.2 on record because of leaving it paused a couple of times).
Okay, I'll throw this game a single bone, because it does deserve it. The game has newpaper clippings which you can find (and has a collectible achievement tied to it which just feels awful and out of place with the rest of the game), and each provide a lengthy and interesting insight to the world events that happened leading up to the start of the game. Whoever wrote those newspaper clippings clearly did a good job of researching world events and writing stories around them, and was able to write these stories in an interesting way (to me at least). The game also has a good intro sequence which shows the rise of North Korea into a nation that would actually provide a significant threat to the US. Lastly, the game does have some very nice (product placement) structures - we have shootouts inside and outside of White Castles, Hooters, and a full-on level that takes place inside and outside of a
store. Although most of the US suburbs feel stilted, repetitive, and poorly drawn, the inclusion of stores like these (and all the other product placement items thrown in) does help ground the game with a nice semblance of realism.
Overall, don't play this game. I only got it because it was $2. With the boring sequences and the factually wrong script lines, I'm not even sure it was worth that

Of all the Space sci-fi games I've played, this is easily one of the most satisfying ones I've played in a long time. It delivers on a great Firefly-esque atmosphere, making you feel like some outlaw merc on the fringes of space, saving or sacrificing whomever you choose.
The soundtrack is great, the graphics are quite good, and the gameplay feels incredibly satisfying. From the "float like a butterfly, sting like a scorpion" action of the smaller, faster ships, to the bulky and powerful dreadnoughts, each ship class has a great feel to it.
The story, while not groundbreaking, does it's job well. And the voice acting, while limited, is more than tolerable at the very least.
If you're looking for a super-realistic, newtonian physics based spaceflight simulator, you're at the wrong galaxy. Rebel Galaxy delivers on an incredibly satisfying space cowboy feel, and at a great price too.

Though it has its shortcomings in the story arena, it's really an excuse to join the upgrade treadmill in buying the biggest, nastiest, blow-things-up-est ship you can manage. It's all about playing missions to get money and buy those sweet, sweet weapons and armor upgrades until you have a veritable capital-ship erasing fortress. At the end of the game, I spent a good couple hours just annihilating missions for giggles; very fun!
And a hint if you plan on playing this on easy mode: join the Merchant Guild ASAP. Equip your ship with Null-Grav Boosters. Occasionally they'll have a mission that's worth like 10x the average mission price because you're supposed to obtain materials and deliver them through a blockade. Obtain them by going to the Commodity Market and looking at which station supplies them. Go to that station, buy their stock, and exit the game. When you continue, they'll have restocked. Keep doing that until you have the necessary units, then deliver to the target station. About 30sm from the location, you'll get pulled out of warp. Just engage your boosters and tap deflectors when rockets are about to hit you or you need to recharge the booster. The first time I did this, I made $250k when missions in the area were only $20-30k, and I wish I knew about it way earlier.

So I had one go at this game and I'm already amazed. I survived for only 16 days until everyone of my crew died. My crew consisted of Pavle, Bruno and Marko. Scavanging for stuff was hard since some people went there from before. Our house didn't have any food and it was cold. So I did almost everything to survive. I got a lot of food, medication, and building supplies. I was set to survive for a long time, but raiders. They steal everything. This game is hard and that's more enjoyable. This game even showed me how I'm a monster. Whilst svanging for items, I entered a house and there was an elderly couple. Seeing as to how they were unarmed, I took everything they had and ran, without any second thoughts. The person I used to steal that stuff was Marko (i used him to scavange stuff everytime). He became broken, he refused to do anything, so I had the rest of the team to talk with him. Soon I got another person to join us, Cveta. She didn't last long. Once night approached on the same day she arrived. I took her to scavange some stuff and she died. There was one armed man there who didn't like me snooping into his stuff. Soon after that everone was depressed. Things got harder as well since bandits kept stealing our stuff. I took Bruno for a run since no one wanted to do anything (Marko and Pavle) and I took him to this church. Everyone there was armed. I managed to take out one guy but my weapon broke and the other guy shot me. One the morning came Marko took off and it was just Pavle. I managed to make him survive 1 day until he became depressed and refused to scavange for supplies. Then the last night some raiders came in and they shot him. He got lethally wounded and he didn't make it to see morning.
I was honestly mad at Marko for being depressed from stealing from people (he also had to kill someone before that since I panicked). I liked Bruno since he only thought about surviving, he usually says stuff like "As long as we have supplies, doesn't matter who we kill". On the other hand Pavle and Marko would be sad at what happened and they won't forget about it. This game comes to show you how hard life is at war, and how it can change some people. I will try to survive again, this time with Bruno, Roman and Arica.

It's not Elite: Dangerous. It's something a lot more fun and less simulationist. Also less time-consuming.
Gameplay is two-dimensional, and borrows the idea of the "broadside" from the age of sail. Otherwise, it has most of the thematic elements you'd expect in some form - trading, piracy, factions, side events to stumble across and so on.
One of the things I really like is how "alive" the galaxy is. It's full of miners in asteroid belts, pirates preying on them, distress beacons, mysterious transponders, ancient minefields, and so on. You can come across two hostile fleets fighting it out with no regard for you. Although there isn't Elite's ability to tip the balance of power by your actions, just smaller scale events that make a minor difference to market prices.
Difficulty estimation is occasionally .. surprising. Upgrade your defences first.
The cowboy rock soundtrack makes a nice change from the expected, and there's a feature to drop in your own music.
Plays nicely with an Xbox controller, although you have to quit game to change control modes. Note you only save when undocking!

First of all, this is the first game ever I can remember where I actually viewed the credits, I just had to know who'd made this game, wich says quite alot about my impressions of it. All unknown people for me though, but that doesn't take away any of the splendor of this game.
As a game, I'm overwhelmed that it portraits the war from the view of the civilians. On top of that, it's not an easy game either. My first impressions made me think of the old classic "the lost patrol" in how you experienced your characters:
Always short on food, getting wounds that become worse, never enough equipment (and I really mean never), and even though you know there's probably an end somewhere, it just eludes you. All focus is on what's most important for the moment.
The game layout itself is simple enough, very easy to learn and get used to, but that doesn't mean it is in any way an easy game. On the contrary, no ability to save when you want and re-load (everyting is autosaved as you progress), no difficulty settings to adjust to make certain points of the game easier, and no clear hints as to what to do or what will work actually makes this game all Ironman mode. You're holed up in your house, and you just have to explore your surroundings to get the most out of it, whatever way you can.
As a hoarder in games, I do enjoy gathering and scavanging stuff, but some of the frustration in this game comes from the fact that you never can bring back everything you find, at the most maybe one third. You'll just have to figure out what you for the moment need most and what you can make the most of. Alot of stuff will be left behind.
Finally, there's events as well, so you not only need to feed, rest and make sure there's coffee and tobacco enough for all, but acting in a bad manner towards your neighbours for example might have an impact on your morale.
If you're interested in exploring, managing, crafting and do just whatever it requires to get through each and every day, this most definetly is a game for you. I rate it 10/10, no doubt.

Hitman: Absolution is a pretty fun game if you're into stealth, assassinations, using guns, choking people, etc. Sounds like an interesting Friday night, hmm? In Hitman: Absolution, you play Agent 47, an elite assassin. You play the game in a 3rd-person style, just over 47's shoulder. You can switch which side you want with a mere press of a key, however feels more comfortable, or as the situation dictates.
The game starts off with an opening mission which plays as a sort of tutorial or getting to know the basic mechanics, it's pretty straightforward, try to infiltrate without being seen, if you take anyone out, make sure you don't leave their bodies in plain sight for others to discover, you are given plenty of places to hide bodies, so it's not too cumbersome. Don't be seen, take people out, disguise yourself as a worker, blend in, and make your way to the target. Take out the target, make it look like an accident, hide the body, whatever the case, don't get caught, if you get caught, take out more people and then clean up even more :P
After the intro mission, you are given more targets, cutscenes, storyline, reasons, blah blah blah... It's not a deep story, basically, you are hired to assassinate an agent who has gone rogue, you find out they were protecting someone. You realise it is up to you to fulfill their work. You go rogue, you rescue the person, you protect them, but others are after them, you take them somewhere else, chaos ensues, in the midst of it all, they get taken. You have to get them back, target, target, target, one step closer, closer, etc...
Regardless of the not-so-deep story, it is still a very enjoyable experience playing. Assassinations are quite satisfying, I must say. And quite a variety of ways to reach your goal, as well as a very open world for a lot of the levels. Wearing disguises and obtaining weapons, whether they be guns, explosives, melee items, etc. is quite enjoyable...
The environments, especially on Ultra graphic settings, are quite spectacular, especially as this game is nearly 4 years old. Looking off into the distance, you really get a feel for the scale, and it often feels quite big and even expansive.
I've played about 35 hours, playing through the storyline 3 times, as well as side-contracts, and have gotten 100% achievements, yet there is still much more to do, there are nearly 300 challenges during the story, which I have only done about half of. There is so much more to do even after my goal of 100% achievements. I will probably go through it a couple more times yet, for it is very satisfying to play... 8.5/10
EDIT: Sept 18th, 10 days later, put in another 25 hours on top of the 100% achievement game... finished all the challenges, found every gun and melee weapon and random object in every level, also completing every level to 100% ...however, the game is not completely done 100%, as some items in the Safe House are locked and can only be purchased by playing contracts and earning money... and then upgrades are locked as well, so, we'll see, might do a bunch of contracts over and over and over until I have the millions of dollars required...

[h2]The Good:[/h2]
* Beautiful graphics, even without the texture pack, pumping all the sliders to maximum produces some very pleasing pixels.
* Strikes a good simulation / arcade balance, most of the time your car behaves the way you would expect it to, very occasionally they seem to have far to much grip, and then some other times none at all.
* Great selection of different cars that sound very similar to the real deal.
* Challenging AI will punish you for almost every mistake, and will make you fight for every position.
* Clean and Intuitive User Interface, not as "pretty" but far more usable than the dirt games.
* Varied game modes that I, personally, will take a while to master, Touring and Street racing are my favourites, and the Endurance, Drifting and Open Wheel events are quite challenging (maybe not open wheel for F1 vets?)
[h2]The Bad:[/h2]
* AI that disobeys the rules the player must stick to, quite a few times I've been tailgating an AI opponent and been penalised for going off track, with the AI racing off ahead of me.
* The game lacks personality, the DiRT 2 and 3 games were brimming with character and style, that could be a little cheesy, but enjoyable. This game feels barren in comparison.
* Could Ravenwest win a few less competitions next time ;-)
* I feel that the multiplayer and singleplayer "career" progression should have been the same, or could even have been tied together (without needing to play both to progress of course.) Missed opportunity there!
[h2]The Ugly:[/h2]
* Nearly everybody before me has said so, I feel I must also stress those car interiors. With nearly everything else about this game been so nice to look at, going inside the cars can be a bit of a shock to the system. While not a complete deal breaker, it was definitely disappointing seeing how bad they looked for the first time.
* Turning off the HUD for full immersion is likely to see you hit a wall (in-game, not figuratively).
[h2]Overall:[/h2]
It's a solid racing game, it doesn't do anything truly great, or really bad.

Before deciding to write a review I tried to fix the issue. Using the all-mighty Google I attempted several fixes that others credited with saving their copy of Bioshock Remastered. This game can be fun to play, but overall, I've found it to be a waste of my time. The big gripe I have about GRID 2 surrounds the difficulty settings. NORMAL is too easy for me (I win every race), but when I move it up to HARD, there are races that are virtually impossible to win. 95% of the time, I start in the back third of the grid at the beginning of the race (in 200+ races, I’ve started on the front row ONCE, and I believe it’s the only time I’ve started in the front two rows), and by the time I fight my way through the traffic into 2nd place, the guy in 1st (who almost always started on the front row) is 5-10 seconds ahead of me.  I normally race well enough to gain on him, but that huge lead he gets off the front row (while you are being held up by the rest of the field) is insurmountable, because he never makes a mistake.  This is especially the case in the coastal/mountain races (point-to-point vs. circuit).  I also find a few of the vehicle challenges to be too difficult on HARD.  I wouldn’t have too much of a problem with it if you could fail on one vehicle challenge and move on to the next, but say you have three challenges and you can’t get past the first one – you can’t move on to the other two.  A new vehicle challenge doesn’t become available to run until you’ve passed the one before it.  So you could end up missing out on multiple cars, because you can’t get past one challenge.  If you could choose each challenge individually, that would solve the issue as far as I’m concerned.  I’d miss out on some cars because I couldn’t earn them (or didn’t want to waste two hours trying to get a perfect run in), but at least I wouldn’t be missing out on cars that had nothing to do with the challenge I couldn’t pass.

Crea isn't worth your time or your money. It's deeply flawed in every major aspect of the Terraria-like genre. There's no incentive to build anything. There's no incentive to explore. There's no joy in spelunking. There's no functioning combat system. There's no point in the talent system or the level system, other than pad the grind time. There's no functioning boss system. Crea is glitched and bugged out the wazoo.
The game fundamentally misunderstands what the point of these types of games are.
First, the game isn't working properly on a technical level. There are game crashing bugs, there are skill bugs, there are map bugs, there are multiplayer bugs. Fighting bugs makes the combat system unplayable.
You'll run into lag in multiplayer, where the players exploring will cause the entire game to just stop doing anything while it's generating the new environment. You will run through empty caves where no minerals have yet spawned, no chests have appeared, no enemies appear and where you can't dig or place torches because the game is lagging behind too heavily. Then you'll hear your multiplayer companion swear over skype because they're suddenly unable to do anything.
Secondly, the building and crafting portion of the game is completely unnecessary. You're delegated to progressing through the standard crafting tiers through the standard way of upgrading your standard crafting stations, getting the standard four weapons and the standard three armor parts. That's it. The rest is reskins with new stats, not changing a damned thing. You use the sword/spear, who work exactly the same, the bow or the wand. Nothing new, nothing exciting, nothing ever changing.
You don't build a base, because why would you? You don't spend any time in your base, you don't have anything to fill your base with, you can take your crafting tables with you instead when you do the arbitrary digging for copper->iron->silver->gold. There's no discovery to be made anywhere along the line.
Thirdly, combat doesn't work. At all. You trigger an enemy's attack, counter, rinse and repeat. Or you shoot at it from afar until it dies. Or, you build a one block wall and hit the enemy through it. This is of course on the rare occasions when enemies spawn at all, and on the even rarer occasion when they're not bugged out. The enemies get progressively higher stats as you walk the planet, but they're the same and their power levels are completely unpredictable. You can be around a lvl 7-9 crystal and suddenly face a lvl 24 enemy. It's stupid.
Fourthly, you never have any goals to strive for. You do, what, exploration? Why? To find what? You don't need anythin, you don't really want to do anything. You dig? Why? To get iron instead of copper for the work station upgrade? Yawn. You come across a red crystal with a dungeon instance? Skip it. Why bother?
Don't get this game. Crea isn't worth it. Get Terraria. Get Starbound if it's on sale. Hell, get Minecraft before you get this. It's no good.
EDIT: I did play the beta 1.4 patch, and that is the version of the game I've reviewed. The beta version of the patch was released on the 7th of June and I played it 3 days later, and my achievments were unlocked on the 10th of June to prove it.

This game has been crashing every 10-15 minutes for me since I got it - I barely made it out of the tutorial map - so I can't really speak to the actual gameplay.  From what I've read there are others with the same issue and it started happening after a game update in October 2015.  After posting details of the problem on the bug report thread (along with what I've done to try and fix it myself), a dev quite promptly responded to tell me they think they've identified a fix and it just needs a bit more testing.  I figured hey, last update was just a few weeks ago, I'm sure they'll patch it soon.
Almost half a year later there have been no patches - fix or otherwise - and now any enquiries regarding fixes for this or other problems get the reply that they're working on the PS4 version of the game and there'll be no updates to the PC version while that's going on.  We'll maybe get a re-port of the PS4 version once it's released, which might fix the issue(s), they think, probably, maybe, but details on any of that are hazy at best.
Obviously there's a lot of people playing the game without issue, so it might be worth a look anyway, but I'd definitely keep Steam's no-questions refund criteria in mind and if you do run into problems go that route immediately rather than wait for the problems to be resolved.

While I've never played Rust, I've researched it and chose that it was not for me.
This is Rust with magic and broomsticks.  Wish I knew that before hand.  Regardless I have enjoyed myself while playing this game, until recently.  Read below for more info, or just skip to the final paragraph.
Graphics- pretty good, could be better.
Sound- The voice chat is a hit or miss, leaning more towards the miss with choppiness and incomprensible speech.
Gameplay- Good, though if you're a melee user then you're garbage.  Melee attacks and spells are the most inferior play style in this game, not to mention the 'Iron' armor tree at this time.
AI- Pretty stupid.  Needs a serious upgrade or even an overhaul.  I tamed a giant and it refused to fight, just staring at me with a constant "Urgh" look on its face.  And fighting wild creatures is horrible.  Sprite, dragons, and orcs are the only real enemies in terms of AI.  Everything else is too stupid to do anything significant.  Orcs for their part are extremely stupid though.  The crossbowmen throw knives instead of shooting arrows/bolts for ♥♥♥♥s sake!  I thought they were arrows till I looked down and saw I got hit by a kinfe, and the melee orcs are somehow worse cuz they can throw three knives at once.  The arc of those knives is pretty bad too.  All in all, the AI are really stupid and need to be redone.
Servers- The connections are garbage.  The server that I played on for most of my time with this game had to restart nearly every hour, and it would be offline for up to 30 minutes or more.  One night it was off for about 4-5 hours.  It was an unofficial server sure, but with the official servers you have no way to naturally regenerate mana.  Kind of a garbage concept if you're playing a mage game like this, you know?  If you're not going to have naturally regenerating mana, at least make some better melee options.
Community- Mixed feelings.  Again, like Rust (probably because many Rust players are now playing this game to an extent).  I was playing on a PvP server and was thinking it would be like the PvP servers of Ark.  In one way it is, in another not at all.  You can walk up to people and not even know who they are which makes any encounter with another player dicey.  You won't know if they are the ones that just raided and killed you, or just some random people trying to play the game.  I myself just got base wiped and I only know two of the people's names cuz they fessed up to it in chat.  The Devs really need floating name tags or something so you don't have to be right up on them and pointed directly at them to know who the ♥♥♥♥ they are.  I've played on that PvP server I mentioned for about 30-31 hours since I bought this game, and for the first 31ish hours the player base was alright.  You had people that thrived in PvP, but most weren't griefing so it was all good.  Then out of nowhere comes the highest level players in the server and they completely base wiped myself and several others merely for giggles.
I realize that the community point is the most lengthy, but that is the main reason that I can not recommend this game.  As long as this game is played by those that enjoy playing as griefers, I can not recommend it in any way, shape, or form.  The game itself has promise.  The current community on the other hand, who can tell?

TL;DR below.
This game should be called 'Grind Galaxy'.
That's because grinding is basically what you will do for 90% (or more) of your game time. Except you're only going to play it for it's main (and only) story. There are no story side quests. Only missions like: destroy some captial ships, rescue a trader by destroying more capital ships, escorting another ship to it's destination while destroying even more capital ships or deliver goods to a certain base which will be hindered by - you guessed right - capital ships which you will have to destroy or run away from.
If you want any challenge out of this game, don't upgrade your ship too much. Do as little grinding as possible, so your missions will stay at least at normal difficulty. The game tells you the difficulty for every mission going from 'extreme' to 'low'. I did the mistake of grinding for a dreadnaught ship with level 6 equipment and the game became childs play.
The story of this game is very lackluster and demotivating. There was much more potential in it to work with, but the devs didn't build on that. It also ends very abruptly. Even the mediocre story of Freelancer looks like a masterpiece compared to Rebel Galaxy's. I was very disappointed by the story. Especially after the ending.
Trading is a waste of time in this game. It has no real simulated economy and the profit margins are so small that it's just not rewarding. The fastest way to make money is to do side missions which, in basically all cases, come down to combat. And after them you can sell the loot you've got from your fallen foes and still make more money than having bought and traded them.
Mining is even more useless than trading except for the one achievement you can get.
The visuals of the game are okay. They don't make you go 'wow', but at least they're not ugly. But even the old Freelancer can hold up with it. And Freelancer has a greater variety of areas you can visit. In Rebel Galaxy every solar system basically looks the same.
The sound of the game and the appraised soundtrack are okay. The soundtrack might annoy you after some time since it's not very diversified. Too few songs are in the game. At least you can set your own music for the various instances of gameplay.
If you're looking for a space action game and haven't played Freelancer then definitely go for that. Or if you want even more quality check out the Descent: Freespace games. Google for Open Freepace for a improved version of them.
If you've played Freelancer already and are looking for something similar, even if not as good, you could give Rebel Galaxy a try. But better buy it on sale. It's not worth it's full price in my opinion.
If you're looking for a space sim where you can do more than just continuous fighting - like trading, mining, building an empire - you should avoid this game and rather check out the games from the X universe or Elite Dangerous.

A 3D swashbuckling space-themed game with clear influence from Sid Meier's Pirates!.  This is not Freelancer or X3 or Privateer.  You can mine all you want, the game will let you, but you'll be broke.  You won't be building a trading empire.  The main idea is to go look for trouble with the right factions and go line up broadsides against their capital ships.  Just go through the main storyline, grind side missions between storyline missions, upgrade your ship, re-outfit it for the right role and go beat up the enemy until the credits roll.  It's a good time and a decent looking game without outrageous system requirements.
The game does not take itself terribly seriously either, but it doesn't get too cartoonish.  There aren't really any RPG elements to speak of.  There is a faction reputation system, but it's nothing special.  Most people will be friendly with citizens and militia, and enemies with the various criminal factions.  The game certainly allows for play as a criminal, there are criminal-owned bases in all the systems, etc... but you're better off being friendly with the law for the storyline.  I found the combat to be incredibly fun, and the different weapons and the different classes of enemies require different strategies for effective play, so combat can be deep; not exactly oceanic, but enough to engage someone for at least the length of the storyline.  It's also self-paced, the missions give you an indication of the relative "risk" of the mission, so you can grind until the mission is "low risk" or challenge yourself by taking "high risk" missions.  There is also a warrior race of what look like giant badgers so...

You know, I first saw the trailer for this game about 4-6 months ago on YouTube, and thought that it looked pretty cool. I picked it up after seeing about 2-3 hours worth of gameplay from multiple different people, and I'm glad I did. This game has some great potential, and is fun to play now as-is, but I do wish there was more.
It's kind of hard/tedous/ a choir to play solo on certain things, like Knowledge unlocks. There are things that you have to unlock so that you can progress through the game, but so far, at level 12 (my highest of 3 characters), I have almost all the things that are necessary, but very little in the way of weapons and armor. Granted I'm still doing good with the first tier of crafted armor and same tier staff. The game definetly caters to smaller groups of 2 to 3, judging by some videos I have seen from a YouTuber I enjoy, who has a total group size of 3. Being solo it's harder to kill any creature or monster simply because it's only 1 weapon attacking it, and not 2 or 3. While that isn't a big issue for lower tier monsters, I can see it being a problem trying to kill any of the "bosses", but that I mean any monster that has tens or dozens of thousands of HP, luckaly they aren't nearly as common as the typical Blood Ork or Wolf or Bear. If there was one thing that I would change right now, it would be to add 1 extra Knowledge per level. It would help going solo so much, and make the game more fun. I don't know if that would make it OP at end-game, but it would make it sooooo much more fun getting there.
The building is quite nice, it works well most of the time, and has a great look. There have been times where it took a minute to get a certain item exactly the way I wanted, but nothing major.
Combat is simple, very simple. You can have up to 2 Spells bound to your weapon, left click and right click, and other than that you honestly just have to watch your Health and Mana, and drink a potion to replenish either. Those potions are very cheap, too. At least at lower levels, like me. Also, maybe it's just me, but the Staff seems much better than the other weapons. The Wand is fast, but not so fast that I would choose it over the Staff, haven't tried the Melee, but I'd rather have range in this game since almost everyone else is using the staff, and the Gauntlets from the very very little I have seen, seem are DoT weapons, and are good at the higher tiers, which take a while to get to.
Crafting is your typical crafting, some things require a specific type of bench to be made. (That's one of the items you NEED, and each one costs 2 Knowledge, and there's like 4 or 5 base level ones.)
I haven't messed with taming at all, because I've had to unlock other things that are needed, but from what I've heard in servers and seen in videos, it's also quite important. It's not like ARK: Survival Evolved, in Citadel you only keep them for 15 mins but that can be upgraded with taming scrolls, some of the high level ones count the time per scroll by days, not hours. And you can only tame things within 10 levels of yourself. But like I said, that is what I have heard from multiple people in-game and in videos, not first hand experience.
I can see the game becoming boring if you're solo like me, just because I have a feeling that the more Northern portion of the map will be hard to deal with solo, even with being the right level.
